messages:
Sasha N.: ran a quick fault-injection experiment on the prefetch/prefix cache path this morning. summary: overall prefix hit-rate down ~12% for llama-2-13b under high-batch workloads, token-saved dropped ~18%. pushed results to the dashboard -> https://console.redwood.internal/d/pcache/experiments (read-only link)
Dev-Bot: experiment run finished: id=exp-2026-03-18-09, injected 5% malformed-keys, toggled kernel-batching thresholds, captured profiler traces
Ben R.: can you paste the profiler flame or a short breakdown? curious if kernel-selection or kv-cache lookup latency is the culprit
Sasha N.: short profiler excerpt:
```
GPU kernels:
  attend_v2: 42ms (40%)
  fused_ffn: 28ms (27%)
  kv_lookup: 12ms (11%)
  memcopy: 8ms (8%)
CPU:
  key-normalizer: 35ms
  cache-lookup-parallel: 20ms
```
Sasha N.: note: the increased memcopy time correlates with larger batch sizes (>=24) where we saw more cache-key collisions/fallbacks
Alice M.: was this concentrated on any route/tenant? or global
Sasha N.: mostly /v1/generate route and a few customers—AcmeCorp and BetaShop are top of the list. per-tenant panel in the dash shows AcmeCorp had 22% hit-rate drop vs baseline
Rick L.: Ops alert fired this AM for token-saved regression :warning: — alert id alert-token-saved-2026-0318
Ops-Bot: alert-token-saved-2026-0318 acknowledged by Rick L.; affected clusters: us-west-2-gpu-pool-3
Ben R.: hypothesis: kernel selection picks a fused path that assumes contiguous KV layouts. when key normalization produces slightly different prefixes under fault-injection, we fall back to non-fused memcopy heavy path. that explains memcopy spike and hit-rate drop together
Ben R.: quick config patch I want to try (small canary):
```
{
  "batching": { "max_batch": 16, "prefetch_threshold": 0.6 },
  "kernel_hint": { "prefer_fused": false }
}
```
Alice M.: +1 to canary. also suggest adding a per-model kernel-path breakdown to the pcache dash (attend_v2 vs attend_v2_fused)
Sasha N.: agreed. action items:
- Ben -> deploy canary config to canary clusters (max_batch=16, prefer_fused=false)
- Alice -> add per-model kernel-path panels + per-tenant token-saved sparkline on the pcache dashboard
- Rick -> increase warmup schedule for AcmeCorp by 3x for next 24h
- Sasha -> run a deterministic fault-injection with key-normalizer toggled and share traces
Rick L.: I'm also going to add a short-run regression alert that watches hit-rate slope over 1h windows and triggers at >10% drop
Sasha N.: copying quick query we used for token-saved delta (feel free to paste into grafana)
```
SELECT
  tenant,
  model,
  route,
  avg(hit_rate) as hr,
  sum(tokens_saved) as ts
FROM pcache_metrics
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '24h'
GROUP BY tenant, model, route
ORDER BY ts desc
```
Ben R.: sounds good. if canary confirms kernel hinting is the fix we should fold into batching heuristic (prefer_fused only when key-normalizer entropy < X)
Alice M.: noted, I'll sketch the dashboard layout and post a screenshot in this thread
Sasha N.: thanks all. I'll post final experiment artifacts (traces + raw profiler) in the thread once uploaded to the artifact store: s3://redwood-artifacts/pcache/exp-2026-03-18
Rick L.: rolling back nothing yet, waiting on canary. :thumbsup:
Sasha N.: pinging @Ben R. when can you deploy the canary? ideally next 30m
Ben R.: can do in ~20m, will report back with short run results
Sasha N.: sweet, closing loop when we have canary numbers.
